safety_verdicts.content: Patient reports numbness of the left arm for 2 weeks.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts document left arm numbness/tingling but do not include the duration of 2 weeks.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the 2-week duration of left arm numbness reduces the ability to localize and risk-stratify the neurologic complaint (e.g., acute vs subacute process), which can affect urgency and differential diagnosis. However, the presence of numbness/tingling itself is still captured, limiting the harm.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient has tingling and numbness in the shoulder.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts do not mention tingling/numbness in the shoulder.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to document shoulder numbness/tingling can impair anatomic localization (e.g., peripheral nerve vs radiculopathy vs central causes) and may change downstream evaluation. This is unlikely to directly cause major harm by itself but can contribute to suboptimal assessment.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Ibuprofen is not listed in generated medications.

The likely outcome is additional monitoring/counseling rather than severe injury in most cases.
